column6: Both paragraphs convey the same core idea about doctrine as central truths rooted in Scripture and lived out by believers, with no significant changes in meaning or intent.
column7: Doctrine simply means the core truths we believe and teach-truths passed on by faithful people of God, rooted in Scripture, and lived out in our daily walk.
column8: Teaching, in the simple sense, means the central truths we believe and teach—truths that have been transmitted by God’s faithful people, rooted in Scripture, and lived out in our daily conduct।

column6: The original uses 'doctrine', which implies a formal set of beliefs, while the back-translation uses 'teaching', which can be broader and less formal. This change affects the doctrinal emphasis of the instruction given by Jesus.
column7: When Jesus instructed His church to ‘teach’, He was instructing them to share His doctrine.
